title: Fast-track shadowing lane + temporary stability pin for urgent customer model onboarding
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Summary:
Many enterprise customers escalate requests to add or pin a particular model variant because of regulatory audits, contractual SLAs, or reproducibility guarantees. Current catalog onboarding is optimized for standard intake lanes (fastpath, staged), but lacks a documented, auditable fast-track lane that preserves platform stability while providing temporary guarantees to customers.

Goal:
Create a short-lived, auditable 'urgent fast-track' flow that allows product and engineering to: (1) shadow-evaluate a customer-supplied model variant against production traffic, (2) apply a temporary stability pin (time-boxed), and (3) capture objective compatibility signals and comms artifacts before converting to a normal catalog lifecycle (pin, deprecate, onboard). The flow must surface regressions quickly, require explicit security and SRE sign-off, and include a standardized customer communication plan.

Outcomes / Acceptance criteria:
- A clear triage checklist for qualifying a request as 'urgent fast-track' (customer SLA level, regulatory requirement, executive sponsor).
- A documented shadowing policy: traffic percentage cap, duration, metrics to record (latency delta, token cost delta, hallucination/regression count on a pre-defined eval set, embedding drift), and failure thresholds that trigger rollback.
- A temporary pin policy template: maximum duration (e.g., 90 days), automatic expiration, renewal process, and telemetry required for renewal.
- An audit template (Confluence) capturing decisions, sign-offs (PM, Security, SRE), and links to PRs/dashboards.
- Playbook for customer-facing comms for acceptance, expiration, and deprecation notifications.
- Implementation plan with minimal console UI changes: a one-click "Fast-track shadow" toggle on catalog request + automatic creation of a shadowing job and alerting hooks.

Metrics to collect during shadowing (minimum):
- 95th and 99th percentile token-latency delta vs baseline model
- Cost per 1k tokens delta
- Eval-set accuracy/regression rate (pre-shared customer prompt set)
- Embedding cosine drift and downstream rerank fidelity drop
- Crash/error rate and OOM occurrences

Risk and mitigations:
- Risk: Shadowing could surface high error rates that affect shared infra quotas. Mitigation: traffic cap and dedicated isolated pool for fast-track jobs; automatic circuit-breaker (ENG ticket).
- Risk: Security/have PII in customer test prompts. Mitigation: require Security review and explicit KMS scope; redact logs for shadowing jobs.
- Risk: Customer expects permanent pin after temporary window. Mitigation: explicit SLA in comms, escalation path to enterprise success, and a formal conversion playbook.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (design): finalize triage checklist, metrics list, and audit template. Owner: PM.
- Week 2 (implementation): small console changes + shadow job orchestration and dashboard wiring. Owner: ENG.
- Week 3 (pilot): run 2 pilot fast-track requests with consenting customers; collect feedback. Owner: PM + Solutions Eng.
- Week 4 (adjust + launch): refine playbook, publish Confluence template, and announce to Sales/CS. Owner: PM.

Documentation and artifacts:
- Confluence template: "Fast-track Model Intake + Temporary Pin" (link below).
- GH PR stub for console toggle and shadow job: (link below).
- Dashboard: temporary "Fast-track" board in Console with per-request metrics and a renewal flag.
